'''Fuad Fares'''  ({{langx|he|פואד פארס}}) is an Israeli [[biologist]] and [[pharmacologist]]. Fares is a professor at the [[University of Haifa]], works at the ''Carmel Hospital'' and was a partner at the ''Biomed Prolor company''.<ref>[https://carmel-ltd.haifa.ac.il/index.php/explore-tech-inn/huresearchers/164-fuad-fares Fuad Fares in Carmel Hospital website]</ref><ref>[https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-1000838903 Scientist behind Prolor: Dr. Fuad Fares]</ref>

== Biography ==
Fuad Fares was born in the village of Hurfish in 1955. He graduated with a bachelor's degree in biology in 1977 from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] and a master's degree in [[medical sciences]] in 1983 from the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]]. In 1987 he completed his doctorate in pharmacology at the Technion. He did his postdoctoral fellowship in the Laboratory of Pharmacology and Molecular Biology at the [[Washington University in St. Louis]]. He is currently an associate professor in the Department of Human Biology at the University of Haifa.<ref>[https://www.israel21c.org/meet-6-druze-leaders-changing-israel-for-the-better/ Meet 6 Druze leaders changing Israel for the better]</ref>

Fares was one of the founders{{when|date=August 2021}} of the public biotechnology company Prolor and he is one of the directors in the company. Prolor was acquired by [[OPKO Health]] in 2013.<ref>[https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-1000838565 Opko Health acquires Prolor Biotech for $480m]</ref> He is married and has four children.<ref>[https://che.org.il/wp-content/uploads/2012/04/קורות-חיים-פואד-פארס.pdf Fouad Fares Resume]</ref>
